parsedVerdict.reasoning:
PlaceOrderUseCase.execute does what an application-layer use case is meant to do. It checks the shape of the incoming PlaceOrderRequest and orchestrates the domain: it reserves stock through the StockReservationService port, builds Order and OrderItem domain objects, saves the order through the OrderRepository abstraction, and maps the result to a DTO.

The file has no persistence, transport or framework code. There is no SQL, no HTTP request or response handling, and no framework decorators. The repository and ID generator are injected domain abstractions.

The validation only checks types and presence on untrusted input: the typeof and Array.isArray checks, and that productId is not empty. That is normal command validation at the application boundary, not domain business logic. Quantity and any other business rules are left to the OrderItem and Order constructors. Requiring at least one item could arguably be an invariant that Order should enforce. But here it is written as an input-shape check, and it does not replace or contradict the domain's own rules, so it does not count as a responsibility from another layer.
